name: Macrobenthos
description: The macrobenthos - big bottom-dwelling invertebrates (polychaete worms, bivalves, gastropods, small crustaceans) of the soft mud; data come from the Sine-Saloum invertebrate compartments refined by local isotope work. It is the most-eaten prey of the whole web - birds, crabs and fish of every guild feed on it - and the study flags it as the ecological linchpin of this turbid mangrove system. Functional group pooling the source's Macrobenthos compartment.
